questions.title: Sidecar container with a shared volume
questions.text:
In namespace `pipeline` create a Pod named `logger` with two containers that share an `emptyDir` volume named `logs` mounted at `/var/log/app` in both:

- container `app`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c "while true; do date >> /var/log/app/app.log; sleep 5; done"`
- container `log-shipper`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c "tail -F /var/log/app/app.log"`

Both containers must be running.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: logger
      namespace: pipeline
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        emptyDir: {}
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do date >> /var/log/app/app.log; sleep 5; done"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/app
      - name: log-shipper
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/app/app.log"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/app

Start from `kubectl -n pipeline run logger --image=busybox:1.36 $do -- sh -c ... > logger.yaml`, add the second container and the volume, then `kubectl apply -f logger.yaml`. Check with `kubectl -n pipeline get pod logger` (READY 2/2) and `kubectl -n pipeline logs logger -c log-shipper`.

references.title: Communicate Between Containers in the Same Pod Using a Shared Volume

checks.hint: container log-shipper must use busybox:1.36

questions.title: CronJob and a manual run
questions.text:
In namespace `batch`:

1. Create a CronJob `cleanup` that runs every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`) with image `busybox:1.36` and command `sh -c "echo cleaning; sleep 5"`. It must never run two jobs at once (`concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`), keep 2 successful and 1 failed job in history.
2. Trigger it once by hand: create a Job named `cleanup-manual` from the CronJob and make sure it completes.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n batch create cronjob cleanup --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/10 * * * *" $do -- sh -c "echo cleaning; sleep 5" > cleanup.yaml
    vim cleanup.yaml     # add under spec: concurrencyPolicy: Forbid, successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 2, failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
    kubectl apply -f cleanup.yaml
    kubectl -n batch create job cleanup-manual --from=cronjob/cleanup
    kubectl -n batch get job cleanup-manual -w

The three history and concurrency fields sit directly under `spec` of the CronJob, next to `schedule`, not inside `jobTemplate`.

references.title: Running Automated Tasks with a CronJob

checks.name: cleanup
checks.hint: cronjob cleanup: schedule */10 * * * *, image busybox:1.36

checks.name: cleanup
checks.hint: cronjob cleanup must set concurrencyPolicy Forbid, successfulJobsHistoryLimit 2, failedJobsHistoryLimit 1

checks.name: cleanup-manual
checks.hint: job cleanup-manual must be created from the cronjob (kubectl create job --from=cronjob/cleanup) and complete

questions.title: Persistent volume claim with an init container
questions.text:
In namespace `storage`:

- create a PersistentVolumeClaim `data-pvc` requesting `1Gi`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce`, storage class `standard` (it provisions dynamically)
- create a Pod `web-data` with an init container `init-html` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c "echo Hello from init > /work/index.html"`) that mounts the claim at `/work`, and a container `web` (image `nginx:1.27`) that mounts the same claim at `/usr/share/nginx/html`

The claim must be Bound and the pod Running.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      name: data-pvc
      namespace: storage
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      storageClassName: standard
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: web-data
      namespace: storage
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-pvc
      initContainers:
      - name: init-html
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello from init > /work/index.html"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /work
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.27
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html

`kubectl -n storage get pvc,pod` should show the claim Bound and the pod Running once the init container has finished.

references.title: Configure a Pod to Use a PersistentVolume for Storage

checks.name: data-pvc
checks.hint: pvc data-pvc: 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName standard

checks.name: data-pvc
checks.hint: pvc data-pvc must be Bound

checks.hint: pod web-data needs init container init-html (busybox:1.36) mounting the claim at /work

checks.name: web-data
checks.hint: container web (nginx:1.27) must mount the claim at /usr/share/nginx/html

questions.title: Parallel Job
questions.text:
In namespace `batch` create a Job `image-resize` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c "echo resizing; sleep 3"`) that runs **4 completions**, at most **2 in parallel**, gives up after **3** retries (`backoffLimit`) and never restarts its containers.

Wait until it shows 4/4 completions.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n batch create job image-resize --image=busybox:1.36 $do -- sh -c "echo resizing; sleep 3" > job.yaml
    vim job.yaml      # under spec: completions: 4, parallelism: 2, backoffLimit: 3 (restartPolicy Never is already there)
    kubectl apply -f job.yaml
    kubectl -n batch get job image-resize -w

`completions`, `parallelism` and `backoffLimit` are Job fields (directly under `spec`); `restartPolicy` lives in the pod template.

checks.name: image-resize
checks.hint: job image-resize: completions 4, parallelism 2, backoffLimit 3, image busybox:1.36, restartPolicy Never

checks.name: image-resize
checks.hint: the job must reach 4 successful completions (give it a few seconds)

questions.title: Rolling update and rollback
questions.text:
Two Deployments in namespace `shop` need attention.

1. `api` must roll out image `nginx:1.27` without ever going below 4 available pods: set its strategy to RollingUpdate with `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0`, then update the image. Record `upgrade api to nginx:1.27` as the change cause.
2. `orders` was just updated to `nginx:1.99`, which does not exist, and its rollout is stuck. Roll it back to the previous revision so it becomes available again.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop patch deployment api -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"RollingUpdate","rollingUpdate":{"maxSurge":1,"maxUnavailable":0}}}}'
    kubectl -n shop set image deployment/api api=nginx:1.27
    kubectl -n shop annotate deployment api kubernetes.io/change-cause="upgrade api to nginx:1.27" --overwrite
    kubectl -n shop rollout status deployment api

    kubectl -n shop rollout history deployment orders
    kubectl -n shop rollout undo deployment orders
    kubectl -n shop rollout status deployment orders

`kubectl edit deployment api` works for the strategy too. `rollout undo` goes back one revision by default; `--to-revision=N` picks a specific one from `rollout history`.

checks.name: api
checks.hint: deployment api must use RollingUpdate with maxSurge 1 and maxUnavailable 0

checks.name: api
checks.hint: deployment api must run nginx:1.27 with change-cause "upgrade api to nginx:1.27"

checks.name: api
checks.hint: deployment api must have 4 available replicas

checks.name: orders
checks.hint: deployment orders must be rolled back to nginx:1.25 (kubectl rollout undo)

checks.name: orders
checks.hint: deployment orders must be available again

questions.title: Canary deployment
questions.text:
In namespace `shop`, Service `web` selects `app=web` and currently sends all traffic to Deployment `web-stable` (3 replicas, `nginx:1.25`).

Add a canary: create Deployment `web-canary` with **1** replica of `nginx:1.27` whose pods carry the labels `app=web` and `track=canary`, so roughly a quarter of the Service traffic reaches the new version. Do not change `web-stable` or the Service.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop create deployment web-canary --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=1 $do > canary.yaml
    vim canary.yaml    # labels app: web, track: canary on the pod template (and matching selector)
    kubectl apply -f canary.yaml
    kubectl -n shop get endpoints web    # 4 addresses: 3 stable + 1 canary

The Service does not know about Deployments, only labels: any pod with `app=web` is an endpoint. The `track` label is what lets you tell (and later scale or delete) the canary separately.

checks.name: web-canary
checks.hint: deployment web-canary: 1 replica of nginx:1.27, pod labels app=web and track=canary

checks.name: web-stable
checks.hint: web-stable must keep 3 replicas of nginx:1.25

checks.name: web
checks.hint: service web must have 4 endpoints (3 stable + 1 canary)

questions.title: Install and upgrade a Helm chart
questions.text:
A chart repository for this lab is published at `https://charts.mockctl.dev/stable`.

1. Add it as repository `stable`.
2. Install chart `stable/podinfo` at chart version **6.4.0** as release `frontend` in namespace `helm-apps` (create the namespace) with **2** replicas (`replicaCount`).
3. Upgrade the release to chart version **6.5.1**, keeping 2 replicas.

The release must end up deployed at 6.5.1 with its Deployment available.
questions.solution:
helm repo add stable https://charts.mockctl.dev/stable
    helm search repo podinfo --versions
    helm install frontend stable/podinfo -n helm-apps --create-namespace --version 6.4.0 --set replicaCount=2
    helm upgrade frontend stable/podinfo -n helm-apps --version 6.5.1 --set replicaCount=2
    helm list -n helm-apps
    kubectl -n helm-apps get deploy

`--set` values are not carried over between upgrades unless you pass `--reuse-values`, so repeat `--set replicaCount=2` (or use a values file with `-f`). `helm history frontend -n helm-apps` shows both revisions.

checks.name: frontend
checks.hint: helm release frontend in helm-apps must be at chart podinfo 6.5.1 (revision 2+) with replicaCount 2

checks.name: frontend-podinfo
checks.hint: deployment frontend-podinfo must have 2 available replicas

questions.title: Kustomize overlay
questions.text:
`~/kustomize/base` holds a Deployment `catalog` (`nginx:1.25`, 1 replica) and its Service. The overlay `~/kustomize/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml` only references the base so far.

Complete the overlay so that applying it creates the resources in namespace `prod` with the name prefix `prod-`, the label `env=prod` on every resource (including selectors), image `nginx:1.27`, and **3** replicas. Apply it with `kubectl apply -k`.
questions.solution:
# ~/kustomize/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
    resources:
    - ../../base
    namespace: prod
    namePrefix: prod-
    commonLabels:
      env: prod
    images:
    - name: nginx
      newTag: "1.27"
    replicas:
    - name: catalog
      count: 3

    kubectl kustomize ~/kustomize/overlays/prod     # preview
    kubectl apply -k ~/kustomize/overlays/prod
    kubectl -n prod get deploy,svc -l env=prod

`replicas` and `images` refer to the names as they appear in the base, before the prefix is added.

references.title: Declarative Management of Kubernetes Objects Using Kustomize

checks.hint: deployment prod-catalog in prod: 3 replicas, nginx:1.27, label env=prod in metadata and selector

checks.name: prod-catalog
checks.hint: service prod-catalog in prod must exist with label env=prod and select env=prod

checks.name: prod-catalog
checks.hint: deployment prod-catalog must have 3 available replicas

questions.title: Readiness and liveness probes
questions.text:
Deployment `payments` in namespace `shop` has no health checks. Add to its container:

- a **readiness** probe: HTTP GET on path `/` port `80`, initial delay 5s, period 10s
- a **liveness** probe: TCP socket on port `80`, initial delay 15s, period 20s

The Deployment must stay available afterwards.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop edit deployment payments

    # inside the container:
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20

    kubectl -n shop rollout status deployment payments

Readiness gates traffic (the pod leaves Service endpoints while failing); liveness restarts the container. Both belong at the container level, beside `image`.

references.title: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes

checks.name: payments
checks.hint: readinessProbe: httpGet / on port 80, initialDelaySeconds 5, periodSeconds 10

checks.name: payments
checks.hint: livenessProbe: tcpSocket port 80, initialDelaySeconds 15, periodSeconds 20

checks.name: payments
checks.hint: deployment payments must stay available

questions.title: Debug a crashing pod
questions.text:
Pod `inventory` in namespace `debug` keeps crashing.

1. Find out why from its logs and save the line that starts with `ERROR` to `/opt/answers/inventory-error.txt` on the base host.
2. Fix it: the container expects the environment variable `DB_HOST`, whose value is in ConfigMap `inventory-config` (key `DB_HOST`). Pods are immutable in that field, so recreate the pod with the same name, image and command plus the variable taken from the ConfigMap.

The pod must be Running.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n debug get pod inventory
    kubectl -n debug logs inventory              # or: logs -p for the previous attempt
    kubectl -n debug logs inventory | grep ERROR > /opt/answers/inventory-error.txt
    kubectl -n debug get pod inventory -o yaml > inventory.yaml
    vim inventory.yaml   # strip status/uid/resourceVersion..., add:
        env:
        - name: DB_HOST
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: inventory-config
              key: DB_HOST
    kubectl -n debug delete pod inventory
    kubectl -n debug apply -f inventory.yaml

`kubectl describe pod` shows the restart count and last state; `logs -p` shows the output of the previous, crashed container.

references.title: Define container environment variables using ConfigMap data

checks.hint: /opt/answers/inventory-error.txt must contain the ERROR line from the pod logs

checks.name: inventory
checks.hint: pod inventory must take DB_HOST from configmap inventory-config key DB_HOST

checks.name: inventory
checks.hint: pod inventory must be Running (recreate it, pods cannot be edited into a new env)

questions.title: Fix a manifest that uses a removed API
questions.text:
`~/legacy/api-deploy.yaml` on the base host was exported from an old cluster and no longer applies here.

Update it to an API version this cluster serves (see `kubectl api-resources`), add whatever the newer version requires, and apply it. Write the API version you used (for example `group/version`) to `/opt/answers/legacy-api-version.txt`.

The Deployment `legacy-api` in namespace `shop` must become available.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -f ~/legacy/api-deploy.yaml     # error: no matches for kind "Deployment" in version "extensions/v1beta1"
    kubectl api-resources | grep deployments      # apps/v1
    vim ~/legacy/api-deploy.yaml
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      ...
      spec:
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            app: legacy-api
    kubectl apply -f ~/legacy/api-deploy.yaml
    echo apps/v1 > /opt/answers/legacy-api-version.txt

Deployments moved to `apps/v1` in 1.16; the old `extensions/v1beta1` version defaulted the selector, `apps/v1` requires `spec.selector` and it must match the template labels. `kubectl explain deployment.spec.selector` confirms the field.

checks.name: legacy-api
checks.hint: deployment legacy-api must be applied as apps/v1 with selector app=legacy-api and 2 replicas of nginx:1.27

checks.name: legacy-api
checks.hint: deployment legacy-api must be available
/opt/answers/legacy-api-version.txt must contain apps/v1

questions.title: Use a custom resource
questions.text:
An operator installed a CustomResourceDefinition for backups on this cluster (API group `data.mockctl.io`).

1. Find the resource and write its **short name** to `/opt/answers/backup-shortname.txt`.
2. In namespace `data` create a `Backup` named `nightly` with `spec.source: pvc/data-pvc`, `spec.schedule: "0 2 * * *"` and `spec.retentionDays: 7`.
questions.solution:
kubectl api-resources | grep data.mockctl.io
    kubectl get crd backups.data.mockctl.io -o jsonpath='{.spec.names.shortNames[0]}'
    echo bk > /opt/answers/backup-shortname.txt
    kubectl explain backup.spec

    apiVersion: data.mockctl.io/v1
    kind: Backup
    metadata:
      name: nightly
      namespace: data
    spec:
      source: pvc/data-pvc
      schedule: "0 2 * * *"
      retentionDays: 7

    kubectl apply -f backup.yaml
    kubectl -n data get bk

The apiVersion of a custom resource is `<group>/<version>` from the CRD; `kubectl api-resources` lists the version and short names.

references.title: Extend the Kubernetes API with CustomResourceDefinitions

checks.hint: /opt/answers/backup-shortname.txt must contain the short name bk

checks.name: nightly
checks.hint: Backup nightly in data: source pvc/data-pvc, schedule "0 2 * * *", retentionDays 7

questions.title: ConfigMap file and Secret environment
questions.text:
In namespace `config`:

- create ConfigMap `app-props` from the file `~/config/app.properties` on the base host (the key must be the file name, `app.properties`)
- create Secret `app-creds` with keys `username=admin` and `password=S3cure!`
- create Deployment `app` (1 replica, image `nginx:1.27`) that mounts the ConfigMap read-only at `/etc/app` and exposes the Secret keys as environment variables `APP_USER` (from `username`) and `APP_PASS` (from `password`)
questions.solution:
kubectl -n config create configmap app-props --from-file=/home/candidate/config/app.properties
    kubectl -n config create secret generic app-creds --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal='password=S3cure!'
    kubectl -n config create deployment app --image=nginx:1.27 $do > app.yaml
    vim app.yaml

    # pod template spec:
        volumes:
        - name: props
          configMap:
            name: app-props
        containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:1.27
          volumeMounts:
          - name: props
            mountPath: /etc/app
            readOnly: true
          env:
          - name: APP_USER
            valueFrom:
              secretKeyRef:
                name: app-creds
                key: username
          - name: APP_PASS
            valueFrom:
              secretKeyRef:
                name: app-creds
                key: password

    kubectl apply -f app.yaml
    kubectl -n config exec deploy/app -- cat /etc/app/app.properties

Quote the password: `!` is special to the shell. `--from-file=<path>` uses the file name as the key; `--from-file=key=<path>` picks another.

references.title: Configure a Pod to Use a ConfigMap

questions.title: Resource requests, limits and a quota
questions.text:
Namespace `limited` has a ResourceQuota `compute-quota`. Inspect it, then create Deployment `worker` there with **2** replicas of `busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600`, where each container requests `200m` CPU and `128Mi` memory and is limited to `500m` CPU and `256Mi` memory.

Both replicas must be running.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n limited describe quota compute-quota
    kubectl -n limited create deployment worker --image=busybox:1.36 --replicas=2 $do -- sleep 3600 > worker.yaml
    vim worker.yaml

    # in the container:
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 128Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 256Mi

    kubectl apply -f worker.yaml
    kubectl -n limited describe quota compute-quota    # Used column moves

A namespace with a quota on `requests.*`/`limits.*` rejects pods that do not set them, so requests and limits are not optional here.

references.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers

checks.name: worker
checks.hint: deployment worker: 2 replicas, busybox:1.36, requests cpu 200m / memory 128Mi

checks.name: worker
checks.hint: container limits must be cpu 500m / memory 256Mi

checks.name: worker
checks.hint: deployment worker must have 2 available replicas

questions.title: ServiceAccount, RBAC and security context
questions.text:
In namespace `secure`:

1. Create ServiceAccount `app-sa`, a Role `configmap-reader` allowing only `get` and `list` on `configmaps`, and RoleBinding `app-sa-configmaps` binding the role to the ServiceAccount.
2. Create Pod `secure-app` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that runs as that ServiceAccount with a pod security context of `runAsUser: 1000`, `runAsGroup: 3000`, `fsGroup: 2000`, and a container security context that sets `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and drops **all** capabilities.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n secure create serviceaccount app-sa
    kubectl -n secure create role configmap-reader --verb=get,list --resource=configmaps
    kubectl -n secure create rolebinding app-sa-configmaps --role=configmap-reader --serviceaccount=secure:app-sa
    kubectl auth can-i list configmaps -n secure --as=system:serviceaccount:secure:app-sa    # yes
    kubectl auth can-i delete configmaps -n secure --as=system:serviceaccount:secure:app-sa  # no

    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: secure-app
      namespace: secure
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 3000
        fsGroup: 2000
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep", "3600"]
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]

`runAsUser`/`runAsGroup`/`fsGroup` are valid at pod level; `allowPrivilegeEscalation` and `capabilities` only exist at container level.

references.title: Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container

app-sa must not be able to delete configmaps
app-sa must not be able to read secrets

questions.title: Fix a Service and expose it on a node port
questions.text:
In namespace `shop`, Service `cart` should route to the pods of Deployment `cart` on their container port `8080`, but it has no endpoints.

1. Fix the Service so it selects the `cart` pods.
2. Make it reachable from outside the cluster as a `NodePort` service on port **30080** (keep port 80 -> 8080).
questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop get endpoints cart                       # <none>
    kubectl -n shop get pods -l app=cart --show-labels        # app=cart, tier=backend
    kubectl -n shop get svc cart -o yaml                       # selector app: carts (typo)
    kubectl -n shop edit svc cart
      spec:
        type: NodePort
        selector:
          app: cart
        ports:
        - port: 80
          targetPort: 8080
          nodePort: 30080
    kubectl -n shop get endpoints cart

Compare the Service selector with the pod labels first; that is where most "no endpoints" problems live. `nodePort` must be within 30000-32767.

checks.name: cart
checks.hint: service cart must select app=cart

checks.name: cart
checks.hint: service cart must have endpoints

checks.name: cart
checks.hint: service cart must be type NodePort with nodePort 30080, port 80 -> targetPort 8080

questions.title: NetworkPolicy for the database
questions.text: In namespace `shop` the pods of Deployment `db` (label `app=db`) listen on TCP `5432`. Create a NetworkPolicy `db-allow-api` so that only pods labelled `app=api` in the same namespace can reach the `db` pods, and only on port 5432. All other ingress to `db` must be blocked; do not restrict egress.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: db-allow-api
      namespace: shop
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: db
      policyTypes:
      - Ingress
      ingress:
      - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: api
        ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 5432

    kubectl apply -f netpol.yaml
    kubectl -n shop exec deploy/api -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 db:5432   # allowed
    kubectl -n shop exec deploy/web-stable -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 db:5432   # blocked

Listing `Ingress` in `policyTypes` with a single `from` rule denies every other source. A `podSelector` without a `namespaceSelector` matches pods in the policy's own namespace.

checks.name: db-allow-api
checks.hint: networkpolicy db-allow-api must select app=db and list Ingress in policyTypes
api pods must reach db on 5432
web pods must be blocked from db on 5432
only port 5432 may be open on db, even for api pods

questions.title: Ingress with two paths
questions.text:
In namespace `shop` create an Ingress `shop-ingress` for host `shop.local` using ingress class `nginx`:

- path `/cart` (Prefix) goes to Service `cart` port `80`
- path `/` (Prefix) goes to Service `web` port `80`
questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop create ingress shop-ingress --class=nginx --rule="shop.local/cart*=cart:80" --rule="shop.local/*=web:80"
    kubectl -n shop get ingress shop-ingress -o yaml

Equivalent YAML:

    apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Ingress
    metadata:
      name: shop-ingress
      namespace: shop
    spec:
      ingressClassName: nginx
      rules:
      - host: shop.local
        http:
          paths:
          - path: /cart
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: cart
                port:
                  number: 80
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: web
                port:
                  number: 80

With `kubectl create ingress`, a trailing `*` on the path means `Prefix`; without it the pathType is `Exact`.

checks.name: shop-ingress
checks.hint: ingress shop-ingress must use ingressClassName nginx and host shop.local

checks.name: shop-ingress
checks.hint: path /cart (Prefix) must route to service cart port 80

checks.name: shop-ingress
checks.hint: path / (Prefix) must route to service web port 80
